note:
The SELFIE variant of the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json, section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm, 2026-08-25: same principles as the full-face wave, but cast ordinary-looking women rather than models, and light it like an amateur phone selfie. All earlier rounds are kept.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST BELIEVABLE VERSION OF THE IDEA SO FAR, AND IT IS NOT MAINLY ABOUT THE CASTING. A studio pair invites the question "who lit this and why", because nobody photographs themselves that way at home. A phone snapshot answers it. The framing device does the work the polish was fighting: crooked framing, wrong white balance, shadow noise, a wide lens enlarging the nose, and eyes aimed at the screen rather than the lens. Casting ordinary faces is the other half - asymmetric features, untidy brows, unstyled hair, no makeup - and the brief states outright that the picture makes no attempt to flatter her.

IT ALSO SOLVES THE VARIANCE PROBLEM PROPERLY. r3 and the full-face wave had to ask for two studio keys that differed "a little", which is a small and slightly artificial difference. Here the two occasions are genuinely different situations - a ceiling fitting overhead versus window daylight; a night-time flash versus a lamp; a warm bulb behind versus a bathroom mirror light in front - so the lighting difference is large, obvious and completely natural. Each slot gets its own pairing.

THE PALETTE DEPARTS DELIBERATELY, AND IT SHOULD BE NOTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DONE. The other waves put her on Acetyl's Pearl grey D8D6D4 studio ground per the concern-to-colour map. A selfie cannot have a studio backdrop without destroying the premise, so the ground is an ordinary home - a bare painted wall, a doorframe edge, tile - kept plain, pale and quiet so it sits near the brand's light ground without pretending to be it. If these ship, the page loses its scene colour on those three blocks. That is a real cost and Malcolm should weigh it.

WHAT CARRIES OVER UNCHANGED:
  * THE HONESTY DEVICE: the number and position of the lines is the same in both panels, NO LINE MAY DISAPPEAR, only depth and shadow change. Magnitude as a fraction of depth - f1 about half, f2 about a third, f3 the smallest but still visible. Session variance applies to the PHOTOGRAPH, never to the FINDING.
  * AND ITS SELFIE-SPECIFIC EXTENSION: she must not come back better GROOMED either. The easiest way for an engine to "improve" an unglamorous woman is to tidy her - makeup, styled hair, better skin tone, a slimmer face. The brief states she has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier or better groomed, and that her under-eye shadows, blotches, scarring and thread veins are unchanged. CHECK THIS FIRST ON EVERY CANDIDATE.
  * NO LETTERING FROM ANY ENGINE, and the wording has now been narrowed TWICE. r3: nbp_pro drew "FIRST VISIT" / "FOLLOW-UP" because the prompt named the panels. Full-face wave: seedream drew "VISIT" even after those labels were removed, because the prompt still said "two clinic visits". So this brief contains the word visit nowhere at all - it says "two occasions", "the earlier day", "the later day". The lesson generalised: ANY caption-shaped noun in a prompt can end up set in type, not just an explicit label. Check the top corners of every candidate.
  * THREE NEW WOMEN, none of them used in any previous wave, so the page never repeats a face.
  * SKIN REALISM SPECIFIED POSITIVELY - pore size varying by zone, asymmetric never-mirrored pigmentation, vellus hair, greasy-to-dry variation. Sheen, glow, dewy and hydrated stay banned.
  * ⚠️ SITE OF MEASUREMENT: all three trials measured the PERIORBITAL region. A full-face frame shows the whole face rather than the site measured, so the block copy and alt text must not imply the figure was measured across the face.
  * ⚠️ RENDER SIZE, MEASURED ON THE FULL-FACE WAVE AND IT APPLIES HERE TOO: the live box is 660px wide on desktop and 350px on mobile, split in two, so each face renders about 330px and 175px. Fine lines are at the edge of visibility at that size and the percentage plate carries more of the message than the picture does. The macro sets did not have this problem. Judge at render size before choosing.

LUMA IS EXPECTED TO REFUSE. It returned HTTP 422 four times across the mouth-chin and full-face waves; it has no negative-prompt field so the negative list folds into the prompt body and trips its filter. Treat a missing luma slot here as expected rather than as a fault to chase.

CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048, each panel a 1:2 portrait.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks  —  selfie, two occasions
slots.prompt:
Two ordinary front-camera phone selfies of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at home, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier one, the right panel is the later one.

THESE ARE AMATEUR SNAPSHOTS, NOT PHOTOGRAPHY. She is holding the phone out at arm's length with its front camera, so: the wide phone lens is close to her face and slightly enlarges her nose and pushes her ears back; the framing is a little crooked and off-centre; the focus is not perfect; there is visible digital noise in the shadows; the white balance is wrong in the ordinary way a phone gets it wrong indoors. Her near shoulder is raised a little toward the camera because her arm is up, but the arm and the phone are OUT OF FRAME. There is no mirror. Nothing about either picture is styled or lit on purpose.

HER WHOLE FACE IS IN VIEW IN BOTH PANELS - head and shoulders, the entire face from above the hairline to the collarbones, nothing cropped off. Both eyes, the nose, the whole mouth and the full jawline are visible. Her expression is flat and self-conscious on both days, mouth closed, not smiling and not posing.

THESE ARE TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. Everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a different day would change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN: the same face shape and jawline, the same nose, the same eye colour, the same brow shape, the same hair colour and the same haircut, and her permanent marks - moles, freckles, sun spots, broken capillaries - in the same places on her face. A viewer must be able to look from one panel to the other and be certain it is one person.

CLEARLY DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO OCCASIONS:
  * LIGHTING - on the earlier day the only light is the ceiling fitting directly overhead, which drops her eye sockets into shadow and throws a hard shadow down from her nose and under her chin; on the later day she is near a window in flat grey daylight coming from one side, much softer and cooler. The two pictures do not look like they were taken in the same conditions.
  * HEAD POSITION - she holds the phone at a different height and angle each time, so the camera is above her eyeline in one and below it in the other, her head is turned and tilted differently, and she sits differently in the frame.
  * EYE GAZE - in one she is looking at her own face on the screen rather than at the lens, so her eyes are aimed slightly low and off to one side; in the other she looks more or less into the lens.
  * BACKGROUND - a different part of an ordinary home each time, plain and uncluttered and softly out of focus: a bare painted wall, the edge of a doorframe, a tiled wall. The wall colour and its brightness are different in each.
  * CLOTHES - a completely different everyday garment each time, in a different colour with a different neckline - the sort of thing worn around the house.
  * HAIR - the same haircut, but unstyled and falling differently: a different parting, flatter on one day, strands out of place, one strand across her face in only one of the panels.

She must never stop being recognisably the same woman, and she must not appear older or younger, heavier or thinner, in one panel than the other.

SHE IS AN ORDINARY-LOOKING WOMAN, NOT A MODEL, AND THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE IN THE PICTURE. Cast her the way a real person looks rather than the way a beauty advertisement casts: she is about fifty, with mousy brown hair scraped back untidily, a round heavy-set face with a broad jaw, small close-set grey eyes under thick untidy brows, a short nose with a bulbous tip, and a ruddy blotchy complexion with broken capillaries across both cheeks and the sides of the nose. She has a double chin and a thick neck. Her features are asymmetric - one eye sits slightly lower than the other, her nose is not straight, and the two sides of her face do not match. She has no makeup, her brows are untidy and unshaped, and her hair is unstyled and a little flat. Nothing about her is glamorous or photogenic, and the picture makes no attempt to flatter her.

WHAT THE COMPARISON IS ABOUT, AND THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the expression lines on her face is the same in both panels and NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Her moles, freckles and broken capillaries are all still there in the same places. What has changed between the two occasions is only HOW DEEP the lines are. She has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier or better groomed - the same ordinary face is simply less deeply creased.

THE SKIN MUST HOLD UP AS REAL AND UNFLATTERED. Pores are clearly visible and vary in size and density by zone - open and obvious through the centre of the face and across the nose, finer at the temples and jaw - with several individual pores larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and asymmetric, never mirrored from one side to the other. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light along the jaw and upper lip. The skin is greasy and light-catching across the nose and forehead and dry at the outer cheeks. No makeup at either occasion, so her lips, lashes and brows are their own natural colour, and her under-eye shadows are her own.

ON THE EARLIER DAY, in the LEFT panel, her expression lines are deeply set even with her face at rest: a fan of four or five creases spreading from the outer corner of each eye, three horizontal lines across the forehead, a pair of short vertical creases between the brows, and a distinct line running down from each side of the nose. In the hard overhead light each one holds a clear shadow along its length.

ON THE LATER DAY, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about HALF as deep - the fold softer, the shadow it holds much lighter, its edges less sharply defined. The deepest ones are still plainly visible. Her moles, blotches and broken capillaries are all still there in the same places.

A snapshot off a phone, not a photograph - slightly soft, slightly noisy, honest and completely unretouched.
